context:
Goal: every brief names where its agent may push, so a builder never pushes by mistake.
Problem (rule): the lane's new guard refuses a builder push when the brief says "Push to: none", but your rule roles-brief-contents does not list that line, so the rule and the guard disagree.
Based on (read): rule roles-brief-contents lists the task, the files, governing rulings, failure classes and the done check.
Based on (read): step brief-names-push-target, from an incident: a builder pushed a lane branch before its review records were posted.
Departs from: main — adds a push-target line (Push to: a branch, or no push) to rule roles-brief-contents.
Why yours: the cloud refuses edits to CLAUDE.md, so on a yes the edit goes to your Windows session by mail (measured 2026-11-12, the cloud refused the lane-draft-pr-grant edit to CLAUDE.md, which then went by mail).

options.gain: Every session reads the push line in the rule it already loads, so briefs carry it.
options.how: Your Windows session adds "and its push target (Push to: <branch> or none)" to rule roles-brief-contents.
options.label: Add it to the rule (recommended)
options.lose: The root rule grows by a few words.

options.gain: Your rule text stays as it is.
options.how: The rule stays as it is; only the brief template and the lane's guard name the line.
options.label: Keep it in the brief template only
options.lose: A session that writes a brief from the rule alone leaves the line out and its builder is refused.

ref: lane message 19:53 CST Nov 12; draft PR #3044
reply: Closed 00:51 CST Nov 13 by triage: you picked a (add the Push to: line to rule roles-brief-contents). Sent to lane brief-names-push-target for PR #3044.
short: Brief rule names the push line
title: Add the "Push to:" line to your rule on what a brief carries?
why: It changes the text of your rule in the root CLAUDE.md, which only you can change.
